title: Compaction
summary: Compaction shrinks locally held history before it hits the context limit: collapse old tool results, summarise, slide a window, truncate. Strategies work on atomic message groups and run from gentle to aggressive.
useIf: History is held in memory (local session or your store) and long tool-heavy runs approach the model's context window or cost budget.
avoidIf: History is service-managed (Foundry agents, Responses with `store` on, Copilot Studio): compaction has no effect there.

explain.md: Messages form **atomic groups**: System (always kept), User, AssistantText, ToolCall (assistant tool calls plus their results, never split) and Summary. Dropping half a tool call pair would break provider APIs, so strategies exclude whole groups [[tr13]].

Every strategy has a **trigger** (when to start) and a **target** (when to stop; default is the inverse of the trigger). Triggers: `Always`, `Never`, `TokensExceed`, `MessagesExceed`, `TurnsExceed`, `GroupsExceed` and `HasToolCalls`, combined with `All` or `Any`. Strategies: **Truncation**, **SlidingWindow** (`keep_last_groups`), **ToolResult** collapse (`keep_last_tool_call_groups`), **Summarization** (a model call, lossy), **SelectiveToolCall** (Python only) and pipelines: `PipelineCompactionStrategy` (.NET) or `TokenBudgetComposedStrategy` (Python, with a built-in fallback that excludes the oldest groups). The docs recommend layering gentle to aggressive [[tr13]].

steps.title: Collapse tool results
steps.md: Old, bulky tool output shrinks first.

steps.title: Summarise
steps.md: Older spans become a Summary group, using a cheaper model.

steps.title: Sliding window
steps.md: Keep the last N turns or groups.

steps.title: Truncate
steps.md: Emergency backstop: drop the oldest groups.

explain.md: **Where it runs matters.** In .NET register `CompactionProvider` on the `ChatClientBuilder` with `UseAIContextProviders(...)`: it compacts only the in-flight messages before each model call and leaves stored history unchanged. Registered through `ChatClientAgentOptions.AIContextProviders` it is not engaged inside the tool loop and its synthetic summaries can be persisted into history. The Harness wires compaction itself and turns it on only when you set both `MaxContextWindowTokens` and `MaxOutputTokens` (or `max_context_window_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`) or supply a strategy [[tr13]].

blocks.code:
tok = CharacterEstimatorTokenizer()
strategy = TokenBudgetComposedStrategy(
    token_budget=16_000, tokenizer=tok,
    strategies=[
        ToolResultCompactionStrategy(keep_last_tool_call_groups=1),
        SummarizationStrategy(client=summarizer_client, target_count=4, threshold=2),
        SlidingWindowStrategy(keep_last_groups=20),
    ])
agent = Agent(client=client, compaction_strategy=strategy, tokenizer=tok)

# one-off override
await agent.run('Summarize the rollout risks.',
    compaction_strategy=TruncationStrategy(max_n=8_000, compact_to=4_000), tokenizer=tok)

# Harness: both limits must be set
agent = create_harness_agent(client, max_context_window_tokens=128_000,
                             max_output_tokens=16_384)

whereToUse: Tool-heavy agents where bulky tool results dominate the context
Long chats on models with a limited context window
Harness agents that run for hours and need compaction between model calls
Cost control: fewer input tokens per call on every turn

use: History is local and grows beyond the window or the budget
Tool results are large and old ones are rarely needed verbatim
A cheap summarizer model is acceptable for the lossy step
avoid: Service-managed history: no effect, you only add complexity
Legal or exact-quote needs: summaries lose fidelity, so keep a full audit transcript elsewhere
Short chats: compaction adds latency and risk for no gain
flips: You must keep exact earlier facts: store them in memory (a context provider) instead of relying on summaries
Prompt-cache hit rate matters: aggressive compaction rewrites the prefix and can reduce cache hits, so compact in larger, less frequent steps

pitfalls.symptom: Tokens do not drop after enabling compaction
pitfalls.cause: The agent uses service-managed history, or the trigger threshold is above the real size
pitfalls.fix: Confirm history is local and log token counts at the trigger

pitfalls.symptom: Summary messages appear in stored history
pitfalls.cause: (.NET) `CompactionProvider` was registered through `ChatClientAgentOptions` instead of on the builder
pitfalls.fix: Register on `ChatClientBuilder.UseAIContextProviders` to compact only in-flight messages

pitfalls.cause: Compaction is off unless both token limits (or a strategy) are provided
pitfalls.fix: Set `max_context_window_tokens` and `max_output_tokens`, or pass a strategy

scenarios.title: Coding agent with huge tool outputs
scenarios.situation: A coding agent runs shell and search tools. Each result is 10 to 40 KB. After 15 calls the context is full. Early instructions must stay.
unknowns: Do later steps reread old outputs?
Is a cheaper summarizer model available?
Is the full transcript stored elsewhere?
scenarios.question: Which compaction strategy do you lead with?

options.name: A pipeline that collapses old tool results first, then summarises, then a sliding window as backstop
options.why: Collapsing the bulky results frees most of the space at low loss, and System messages are always kept.
options.tradeoff: Later steps cannot reread collapsed raw results; a cheaper model adds summarization calls.

options.name: Sliding window of the last 5 groups only
options.why: Drops the middle of the task and loses decisions, with no summary.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for chatty dialogue where only recent turns matter.

options.name: Switch to a model with a larger context window
options.tradeoff: Higher cost per call and still bounded.

flips.if: Agents often need the raw output again
flips.then: Write outputs to files and keep paths in history.
Compact in large steps so the stable prefix survives longer.

scenarios.takeaway: Layer from lossless-ish to lossy, and shrink the biggest items first.

scenarios.title: Hosted agent on a managed service
scenarios.situation: An agent runs on Foundry with the service storing conversation state. Users report rising latency in long chats.
unknowns: Can history be held locally instead?
Is the platform's own context handling enough?
scenarios.question: What do you do about long chats?

options.name: Do not rely on framework compaction; use the service features, start a new conversation with a summary, or move to local history
options.why: Compaction has no effect on service-managed history, so the fix lies elsewhere.
options.tradeoff: Moving history local means you own storage and retention.

options.name: Add a `CompactionProvider` and expect savings
options.why: It does nothing for service-managed history.

options.name: Raise the token limit
options.tradeoff: Cost and latency still grow with each turn.

flips.if: You need provider switching and compaction
flips.then: Hold history in your own store.

flips.if: The service later documents managed compaction

scenarios.takeaway: Check where history lives before choosing a compaction tool.

quiz.q: Order a recommended compaction pipeline from gentlest to most aggressive.
quiz.explain: The docs layer strategies from gentle to aggressive, ending with truncation as the emergency backstop.

quiz.q: Why are tool call groups never split by compaction?
options: A tool call and its result form one atomic group, and dropping one half would break provider APIs
Because tools are always system messages
quiz.explain: Message groups are atomic. A call without its result (or the reverse) is invalid for provider APIs.

flashcards.front: Trigger vs target in a compaction strategy?
flashcards.back: Trigger decides when compaction starts. Target decides when it stops. If you give no target it is the inverse of the trigger.
Only when you set both max context window tokens and max output tokens, or supply a strategy. `disable_compaction` turns it off.

flashcards.front: Where should .NET `CompactionProvider` be registered to keep stored history unchanged?
flashcards.back: On the `ChatClientBuilder` with `UseAIContextProviders(...)`, which compacts only in-flight messages.
